dotfiles.description: Carol's shell, git and editor configuration. Nothing clever; everything documented.

files.README.md:
# dotfiles

Symlink each file into $HOME with `./install.sh`. Tested on Ubuntu 24.04 and macOS.
files.install.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
for f in zshrc gitconfig; do
  ln -sf "$PWD/$f" "$HOME/.$f"
done
files.zshrc:
export EDITOR=vim
alias gs='git status --short'
alias gl='git log --oneline -20'
setopt HIST_IGNORE_DUPS
files.gitconfig:
[user]
	name = Carol Nakamura
[pull]
	rebase = true
[init]
	defaultBranch = main

replay-tools.description: Command-line tools for recording, shrinking and replaying deterministic simulation runs.

files.README.md:
# replay-tools

Record a run as (seed, inputs). Replay it byte for byte. Shrink the inputs until the
failure is as small as it gets.

    replay record --seed 42 -- ./my-sim > run.log
    replay play run.log
    replay shrink run.log --until 'exit != 0'

Works with anything that reads its clock and randomness from the harness and nothing else.
files.Cargo.toml:
[package]
name = "replay-tools"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"

[dependencies]
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"

files.docs/shrinking.md:
# Shrinking a failing run

1. Record with a seed. 2. Confirm `replay play` reproduces the failure. 3. `replay shrink`.

If step 2 fails on another machine, look for fused multiply-add before you look at anything else:
ARM contracts `a * b + c` by default and x86 usually does not.

1.title: shrink should accept a predicate script, not just an exit code
1.body: `--until 'exit != 0'` is fine for crashes. For a wrong-answer bug I need to run a checker. Proposal: `--until-script ./check.sh`.
1.author: s-kovac

2.title: Recorder warns instead of refusing on --allow-clock
2.body: README says the recorder refuses a program that reads the clock. It warns. One of them is wrong.
2.author: dmorel

comments.author: bmartinez
comments.body: README was wrong; it warns on purpose so you can record a run you know will not replay. Fixed the wording.

notes-cli.description: A tiny notes tool: one Markdown file per day, searchable, no sync, no accounts.

files.README.md:
# notes

    notes            # open today's file in $EDITOR
    notes grep TERM  # search every day
    notes yesterday  # what did I do

Files live in ~/notes/YYYY-MM-DD.md. That is the whole design.

# notes

    notes            # open today's file in $EDITOR
    notes grep TERM  # search every day
    notes yesterday  # what did I do

Files live in ~/notes/YYYY-MM-DD.md. That is the whole design.
files.docs/usage.md:
# Usage

One file per day. If you want folders, tags or sync, this is not the tool.

    notes            # today
    notes yesterday  # yesterday
    notes grep TERM  # every day, sorted by date
